name: Givelight Foundation
mission: Givelight Foundation's primary exempt purpose is to provide shelter, clothing and food to children who have been orphaned by a natural disaster or other global crisis; to provide educational, spiritual and social services to the children residing in these orphanages.
scoreSummary: Givelight Foundation shows strong alignment and moderate impact, with zakat compliance (minor risk deductions applied).
zakatClaimEvidence: All zakat given to GiveLight will be directed towards four major categories: food, clothing & shoes, books, medical needs, and other areas considered a transfer of wealth such as pocket money and saving accounts. Zakat can be paid to the following who fall into one or more of eight zakatable categories designated by God in the Quran (9:60). The poor; The needy; Collectors of Zakat (i.e. GiveLight Foundation); Those whose hearts are to be reconciled (i.e. new Muslims and friends of the Muslim community); Those in bondage (i.e. slaves and captives); The debt-ridden; In the cause of God; The wayfarer, meaning those who are stranded or traveling with few resources. (Source: https://givelight.org/zakat/)

keyConcerns.headline: Operating reserves are calculated from the FY2023 Form 990, not the FY2024 income statement above
keyConcerns.detail: Charity Navigator supplied the more recent income statement but publishes no balance sheet for that year, so reserves are computed from the IRS filing's own assets and expenses. The two figures describe different years and will not divide into one another.

keyConcerns.headline: Zakat-collecting organization holds 135 months of reserves
keyConcerns.detail: Zakat must be distributed promptly per Islamic jurisprudence. Large reserves raise concerns about timely distribution.

keyConcerns.headline: CEO compensation is 5.9% of revenue ($134,108 on $2,270,848)
keyConcerns.detail: For orgs with revenue <$5M, CEO pay above 5% of revenue warrants scrutiny.

keyConcerns.headline: Claims 11 geographic areas but no foreign grants on Schedule F
keyConcerns.detail: Organization lists international operations but IRS filings show no foreign grant activity.

rich_narrative.summary: GiveLight Foundation builds and supports homes and provides education for orphans in crisis zones globally, including Afghanistan, Nepal, Indonesia, and Bangladesh. In FY2024, the foundation reported <cite id="3">total revenue of $2,270,848</cite> and maintains a <cite id="1">90.1% program expense ratio</cite>, allocating the vast majority of its budget to direct service delivery. The organization holds a <cite id="1">92/100 overall score from Charity Navigator</cite> and operates with low fundraising costs of <cite id="1"><$0.01 per $1 raised</cite>. However, financial filings indicate <cite id="1">135.0 months of operating reserves</cite> ($11,280,674 in total assets), which represents a large capital accumulation that may slow the deployment of funds.
